title: Bobble wrap shawl
subtitle: A rectangle of double crochet studded with five-treble bobbles in aran-weight yarn
excerpt: This rectangular wrap uses a dc background with bobbles on every fourth stitch and every fourth row, creating an all-over raised spot texture. The yarn is aran weight on a 5 mm hook. Finished size is approximately 160 cm wide by 55 cm deep. The bobbles form on wrong-side rows so they push outward on the right side.
heroPrompt: A chunky crochet wrap in deep teal aran-weight yarn draped over a wicker chair arm, with the raised bobble texture clearly visible on the front face, photographed in warm afternoon light.

glossaryTerms.definition: Work 5 trebles into the same stitch, leaving the last loop of each treble on the hook (6 loops on hook), then yarn over and draw through all 6 loops. The 5 trebles clump together to form a raised rounded bump on the fabric face.

A bobble worked on the wrong side of the fabric, so that the bump pushes through to the right side when the work is turned. This gives a cleaner right-side appearance than working bobbles on the right side.

content.text: This wrap is a rectangle of double crochet with a five-treble bobble worked on every fourth stitch of every fourth row. The bobbles are made on wrong-side rows, so they push toward the right side as a raised spot when the work is turned. At 160 cm by 55 cm the finished piece is a full wrap with enough depth to fold across the shoulders. Aran weight on a 5 mm hook gives a dense, warm fabric.
A
bobble (5-treble cluster)
is five trebles worked into the same stitch, each left unfinished until the final pull-through. The result is a firm rounded bump. Because the bobbles are
wrong-side bobbles
, each bobble-row is a wrong-side row.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 550 g aran-weight yarn. A 5 mm crochet hook (US H/8). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. Stitch markers (optional, to track bobble positions).

content.text: Gauge

14 dc x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran-weight yarn with a 5 mm hook, measured unstretched. Bobble rows pull the fabric in slightly; swatch at least 20 rows including two bobble rows to get an accurate row gauge.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
bobble (5-tr cluster into one stitch, described above).
Pattern

The wrap is worked flat along its length; the foundation chain is the 55 cm depth and the rows build the 160 cm width. Bobble rows occur on row 3, then every fourth row after that (rows 7, 11, 15, etc.), all of which are wrong-side rows. On bobble rows, work one bobble on every fourth stitch starting at stitch 4, with dc between each bobble.
Foundation chain
Ch 78. (This gives 77 working stitches across the 55 cm depth.)
Row 1 (right side, plain)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch throughout). 1 dc in each ch across. Turn. (77 sts)
Row 2 (wrong side, plain)
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Turn. (77 sts)
Row 3 (wrong side, bobble row)

Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in each of first 3 sts. *Bobble in next st, 1 dc in each of next 3 sts*; repeat from * to * to last 2 sts. 1 dc in each of last 2 sts. Turn. (58 dc, 19 bobbles = 77 sts)
Rows 4 to 6 (plain)
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Turn. (77 sts each row)
Row 7 (wrong side, bobble row, offset)

Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in first st. *Bobble in next st, 1 dc in each of next 3 sts*; repeat from * to * to last 4 sts. Bobble in next st, 1 dc in each of last 3 sts. Turn. (57 dc, 20 bobbles = 77 sts)
Note: the bobble offset on row 7 places the bumps between those of row 3, creating a brick-pattern texture rather than a vertical column.
Continue to approximately row 225

Continue the four-row sequence: 3 plain rows, then 1 bobble row (alternating the row 3 and row 7 bobble offset). Work until the piece measures 160 cm from the foundation chain edge, approximately 225 rows. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in both ends securely through the back of several stitches. The bobble texture does not require blocking to show the pattern, but wet-blocking to the finished measurements will even out any tension differences between plain rows and bobble rows. Pin flat and leave to dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat to dry on a clean surface; the bobbles can be gently shaped by hand while the fabric is still damp.
What to try next

Work the bobbles in a contrast colour by joining a second shade at the beginning of each bobble row, then changing back to the main colour on the next row. A puff stitch (worked the same way but with yarn-overs rather than full trebles) gives a rounder, softer raised shape. The same rectangle in DK weight on a 4 mm hook produces a finer bobble texture for a lighter wrap.
